title_ja: 高齢者を食い物にする｢外貨建て保険｣に潜むワナ 販売手数料稼ぎ狙った回転売買が銀行で横行
summary_en: Toyo Keizai feature describing a customer in his 70s at a regional bank urged to cancel a dollar single-premium policy and buy again, arguing that such churning generates commissions. It describes one case and does not give industry data in its open part.

title_en: Dai-ichi group: seconded employee at agency Iric sent policy data to Neo First Life (Iric release of 8 Aug 2024)
publisher: アイリックコーポレーション
summary_en: Agency Iric Corporation said on 8 August 2024 that a Dai-ichi Life employee seconded to it had leaked information on its customers' life, non-life and small-amount policies to Neo First Life, which Iric learned of from Neo First on 2 August. The data were insured names, insurer names, birth dates and policy numbers for about 72,000 people; Iric said there was no onward leak and that it had reported to the relevant authorities.
title_ja: お客様の契約情報等の漏えいについて
日本生命、代理店出向を停止　不祥事受け商慣行見直し
title_en: Nippon Life halts agency secondments, reviews business practices after misconduct
summary_en: Nikkei reports Nippon Life will in principle end placing its staff at sales agencies and banks, the first life insurer to do so as reported, and aims to have no seconded staff in sales or sales support from fiscal 2026. About 50 people were seconded as of April.
note: page read (members-only article; only the open introduction was readable)

title_en: Nippon Life to end bank sales staff placements
summary_en: Reports Nippon Life is phasing out placing employees in the sales teams of banks and other firms, citing competition and fairness concerns. It had 51 staff on such arrangements and is discussing moving them to non-sales work or ending the placements. The article notes the non-life association's earlier ban on such dispatches.

title_ja: 日生に報告徴求命令 金融庁、出向者持ち出しで
title_en: FSA orders Nippon Life to submit a report over information taken by seconded staff
summary_en: Nippon Life said on 18 July 2025 that it had received an FSA report order under Article 128(1) of the Insurance Business Act over the case it disclosed on 16 July, in which a staff member seconded to a bank took the bank's internal material (its evaluation scheme and rival insurers' product revisions) in March 2024 and sent it to Nippon Life. Nippon Life's releases do not name the bank.
note: link dead; facts from Nippon Life releases of 16 and 18 July 2025

verified.how: second source: Nippon Life releases of 16 and 18 July 2025 (nissay.co.jp/kaisha/news/20250716.html, 20250718.html)

title_ja: 日本生命、無断持ち出し600件 銀行や代理店への出向者
title_en: Nippon Life: about 600 unauthorized removals by staff seconded to banks and agencies
summary_en: Nippon Life reported to the FSA on 12 September 2025 that staff seconded to seven agencies (banks and others) had obtained 604 items of internal information by improper means between May 2019 and February 2025, such as sales results, staff evaluation criteria and rival products. No customer data and no explicit instruction were found. On 18 November it revised the figures to 600 items, May 2019 to March 2025. It plans to end secondments to sales roles around April 2026.
note: link dead; facts from Nippon Life release of 12 Sept 2025 (updated 18 Nov 2025)

verified.how: second source: Nippon Life release of 12 Sept 2025 (updated 18 Nov) nissay.co.jp/kaisha/news/20250912.html

title_en: Nippon Life uncovers widespread employee information theft
summary_en: Reports Nippon Life found 604 cases from 2019 to 2025 in which 13 employees seconded to seven banks and financial firms photographed and took confidential sales documents. The insurer says it did not order this; disciplinary action was being considered.

title_ja: 今後営業部門への出向は行わない ～ 日本生命からの出向者が不適切に情報取得
title_en: Nippon Life will not second staff to sales departments; seconded staff obtained information improperly
summary_en: ScanNetSecurity reports that on 12 September Nippon Life announced its report to the FSA on information obtained by improper means by staff it had seconded, following its 16 July disclosure and the FSA report order it received on 18 July. The headline notes the company will no longer second staff to sales departments.

title_ja: 第一生命HDが出向者による内部情報の無断持ち出しで前言翻し､グループ会社の再調査に着手
title_en: Dai-ichi Life HD reverses course on seconded staff's unauthorized removal of information, begins re-investigating group companies
summary_en: Toyo Keizai reports Dai-ichi Life Holdings is leading a re-investigation of group insurers, after Dai-ichi Life said in July that it had checked the matter the year before and planned no new review. It says the group learned after the August 2024 Iric customer-data leak that secondees had also taken rivals' sales results and product information from Iric, Higo Bank and others, and that removals at 27 agencies were not disclosed.

title_ja: ＜迷走＞出向者による｢内部情報の無断持ち出し問題｣で日本生命が処分内容を一転して開示､その甘さに批判の声が集中
title_en: Nippon Life reverses course and discloses penalties over seconded staff information case; criticism of leniency
summary_en: Reports that on 18 November Nippon Life said staff seconded from it and Nissay Wealth Life had taken over 1,500 items since 2019 but withheld penalty details, then on 25 November disclosed pay cuts and voluntary pay returns for executives. The article says criticism focused on the reversal and on the penalties being light.

title_ja: 情報持ち出し、生保販売に影
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports that after secondees' information removal, the industry association said insurer staff placements at other firms would in principle end, so insurers cannot support bank and agency sales on site and fear lower sales. Banks will keep selling insurance; agencies were about 15% of enrolments in a 2025 survey.

title_ja: 明治安田生命でも情報持ち出し
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Meiji Yasuda found 39 cases of staff seconded to four agencies taking out information, including competitors' sales results, between May 2022 and August 2024, involving 10 people. The company blamed weak knowledge of information handling and plans discipline.

title_ja: 住友生命でも他社情報持ち出し
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Sumitomo Life confirmed 780 cases in which 13 seconded staff took other insurers' product information from eight agencies between April 2022 and May 2025, photographing documents on personal phones. The company denies ordering it and will withdraw seconded staff by end of March.

title_ja: 住友生命も780件持ち出し 生保大手4社に拡大、独禁法リスク
title_en: Sumitomo Life also took 780 items; spreads to four major insurers; Antimonopoly Act risk
publisher: Tokyo News Media (東京報道新聞)
summary_en: Reports that some data taken was competitively sensitive, and quotes experts as saying the conduct might raise Antimonopoly Act issues (interference with transactions) as well as trade-secret questions. It also says up to about 50 people at Sumitomo Life may have seen the data.
note: page read (small outlet; the antitrust view is attributed to unnamed experts, not a regulator finding)

title_ja: 社員の情報持ち出し１１５５件
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Dai-ichi Life Holdings confirmed 1,155 cases across Dai-ichi Life, Dai-ichi Frontier Life and Neo First Life in which 64 seconded staff at 28 agencies took competitors' product information. Similar cases had been found at Nippon Life, Meiji Yasuda and Sumitomo Life.

title_en: Dai-ichi Life flags widespread unauthorized data transfers at agencies
summary_en: Reports 1,155 incidents involving 64 employees on loan from group insurers at 28 sales agents, some banks, found in a review covering April 2021 to October 2025. Some had been spotted in 2024 but not disclosed. Executives face penalties and the group will stop placing staff at agents for sales by end of March.

title_en: FSA discussion points for dialogue with the Life Insurance Association of Japan (20 Feb 2026)
summary_en: Among the points the FSA raised at its 20 February 2026 meeting with the Life Insurance Association, it called the run of cases at life insurers of information leaks by seconded staff and improper handling of money very regrettable, said it will establish the facts case by case and act strictly under the law where policyholder protection is lacking, and asked management to treat compliance risk as inseparable from the business model.
title_ja: 業界団体との意見交換会において金融庁が提起した主な論点［2026年２月20日開催 (生命保険協会)］
出向先情報、数千件持ち出し疑い メットライフ、国内生保で最多
title_en: MetLife suspected of taking thousands of items from host firms, most among domestic life insurers
summary_en: Kyodo (via Sakigake) reported on 17 March 2026 that MetLife Life was suspected of thousands of cases of staff taking information from the agencies hosting them, possibly more than the about 3,500 found at four large domestic groups (Nippon Life group 1,543, Dai-ichi 1,155, Sumitomo 780, Meiji Yasuda 39). MetLife said it was investigating and would publish results; the FSA was examining the facts.

title_ja: 広島銀行から不正持ち出し８８件
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Hiroshima Bank said a MetLife Life secondee took part of 88 customers' policy information in two printouts in 2021, without contact details or account numbers. MetLife says it did not leak outside the company; the bank ends accepting insurer secondees at end of March.

title_ja: 福岡銀行でも顧客情報持ち出し
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Fukuoka Bank said a MetLife Life secondee took part of the policy data of 1,052 individuals and 45 companies and emailed it to MetLife three times between December 2023 and April 2024. The bank says addresses and account numbers were not included.

title_en: Manulife Life: misconduct case by a former sales employee (release of 31 March 2026)
publisher: マニュライフ生命保険
summary_en: Per search-result summary, Manulife Life said it detected misconduct by one former sales employee on 14 January 2026 and confirmed 52.75 million yen taken from 20 people, which it says it compensated in full.
note: snippet only (the PDF returned 403; Japanese title not seen, so none is given)

title_ja: メットライフに報告命令、金融庁
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reported on 30 April 2026 that the FSA had issued MetLife Life a report order under the Insurance Business Act over suspected improper removal of information by staff seconded to agencies, said to run to thousands of items. The article does not date the order; MetLife's 1 May release says it was received on 26 December 2025. Hiroshima Bank and Fukuoka Bank had already disclosed removals of customer data. Four large domestic groups had about 3,500 cases.

title_ja: ソニー生命に報告徴求命令
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Sony Life said the FSA ordered a report under the Insurance Business Act over suspected defrauding of customers by a sales employee. About 30 customers had made such reports and the company is checking about 2.8 million policies.

title_ja: 出向者の情報持ち出し２４７６件
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports MetLife Life said on 1 May 2026 that seconded staff took 2,476 items from 36 agencies, which Kyodo calls the largest in the domestic industry. Some contained personal data, which MetLife says was not used for selling. It will in principle make no new secondments, and four executives will return part of their pay.

title_ja: メットライフ生命保険も出向者による｢スパイ活動｣／銀行など36代理店から2400件超の内部情報を無断で持ち出し
title_en: MetLife also involved in seconded-staff 'espionage'; over 2,400 internal items taken from 36 agencies including banks
summary_en: Reports MetLife Life's disclosure of 2,476 items taken from 36 agencies between April 2021 and October 2025, many with customer information. It states the FSA issued MetLife a report order in December 2025, after an earlier internal check had missed the problem.
note: page read (paywalled; open part only). MetLife's own release confirms the FSA report order was received on 26 December 2025

title_ja: 保険客１４人から詐取１・２億円
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Sony Life said four sales employees took about 120 million yen from 14 policyholders through unrelated investment pitches and loan requests. It is reviewing all about 2.8 million policyholders and the review followed an employee's borrowing of about 2.2 billion yen from about 100 clients, dismissed in April 2023.

title_ja: 不祥事対策、実効性に課題　生保協会長「十分でない」
summary_en: Kyodo interview in which the new Life Insurance Association chair, Dai-ichi Life's president, says earlier measures against misconduct such as sales staff defrauding customers were not effective enough, and plans customer warnings and ethics training for sales staff. The article cites the Prudential and Sony Life money cases.

title_en: Rate hikes redirect Japan's life insurance buyers toward yen products
summary_en: Reports that as Japanese rates rose, buyers moved from foreign-currency policies to yen single-premium whole life, lifting fiscal 2025 revenue at large insurers, with buyers aged 60 and over prominent. Regulators are monitoring bank-channel sales; one insurer suggested the surge was slowing.

title_ja: ソニー生命で金銭詐取 社員２人が計１５０万円
title_en: Sony Life: two employees defraud customers of 1.5 million yen in total
summary_en: Kyodo reports Sony Life announced two sales employees took 1.5 million yen from customers in total; both were dismissed effective 21 July 2026. It was the first time the company acknowledged outright fraud, after earlier disclosing improper money dealings above 2 billion yen.

title_ja: ソニー生命に立ち入り検討　金融庁、不正の実態把握へ
summary_en: Kyodo reports the FSA is considering an on-site inspection of Sony Life to examine causes of employee misconduct and management oversight, with a business improvement order possible if systemic failings are found.

title_ja: ソニー生命で詐取５千万円
publisher: 共同通信 (via OANDA Lab market news)
summary_en: Kyodo reports Sony Life said on 11 September 2026 that three sales employees had defrauded customers of 54.9 million yen in total. They include a Chiba-branch employee who pitched unlisted shares to 13 customers (33 million yen), whose case was first disclosed on 4 August. Two employees also improperly received 5.5 million yen. The FSA was considering an on-site inspection.

title_ja: ソニー生命に立ち入り、金融庁　不正の原因調査へ
summary_en: Kyodo reports the FSA entered Sony Life under the Insurance Business Act to investigate why employees defrauded customers and how it oversees management. Three sales staff took a combined 54.9 million yen; the company plans a progress update in mid-December.

title_ja: 不祥事連発で“信頼失墜”…金融庁が保険業界に迫る「AI・代理店・再保険」3つの改革
summary_en: Describes the FSA's 2026 Insurance Monitoring Report, which asks the industry to revisit evaluation and pay systems, agency relationships and three-lines management after misconduct cases, and covers AI use and cyber resilience.
note: page read (only the opening section was readable; reinsurance part not seen)

title_ja: 住友生命 健康関連プログラム利用者約8万人分 個人情報漏えい
summary_en: NHK reports Sumitomo Life said unauthorized access at a system-operations contractor leaked personal information of about 80,000 users of its health-related programs, including names and addresses.
